packageRules.description: Routine updates still merge unattended, but RENOVATE performs the merge from inside its own run — `platformAutomerge` is deliberately false. GitHub's platform auto-merge is a per-PR flag any write-access account can arm, and the PR then merges itself later with nobody watching; these rules have no authority over it. On 2026-07-26 a bulk `gh pr merge --auto` sweep armed it across 8 repos and two actions/checkout MAJORS merged with zero reviews the next morning (reddoor-starter#77, reddoor-website#111) once Renovate's rebase cleared their conflicts. Routing merges through Renovate makes these packageRules the actual decision-maker. Renovate can only merge while running, so the repo cron IS the merge cadence (twice daily).

Never auto-merge packages that reshape the dependency graph (and thus pnpm hoisting). An @reddoorla/maintenance minor bump silently broke Netlify builds via an undeclared transitive sharp (fleet sharp fixes, 2026-06): GitHub Actions built green while Netlify failed. Require a human + a green Netlify deploy preview before these merge.

Majors need a human. This rule has been correct since the preset's first commit and was never the failure: Renovate has never armed auto-merge on a major. The 2026-07-26 incident (two actions/checkout majors merged with zero reviews — reddoor-starter#77, reddoor-website#111) came from a bulk `gh pr merge --auto` sweep by an operator/agent, which no Renovate config can block because platform auto-merge is a per-PR flag set outside Renovate. The real guard is that the fleet now disables platform auto-merge at the repository level (see the reddoor-maintenance `self-updating` recipe, which enforces allow_auto_merge=false and reports drift), so every merge goes through Renovate and lands on these rules. `platformAutomerge: false` here is belt-and-braces, not the mechanism.

Hold pnpm at 11.8.x on EVERY surface it appears: pnpm/action-setup's self-installer crashes bootstrapping any pnpm >=11.9 target ('self-installer exits with code 1' / 'Cannot use in operator to search for integrity in undefined'), breaking CI fleet-wide (2026-07). Deliberately NOT scoped to matchDepTypes packageManager — the same dep also surfaces through the github-actions manager as pnpm/action-setup's `version:` input, and holding only one side ships a guaranteed failure: on 2026-08-03 reddoor-maintenance#492 bumped the workflow inputs to 11.18.0 against the held packageManager 11.8.0 and action-setup hard-errors on any version mismatch. (Workflows should not pass `version:` at all — packageManager is the single source of truth — but the hold must not depend on that discipline.) Only non-major pnpm bumps are held; MAJOR pnpm updates and vulnerabilityAlerts still open PRs so the operator is notified for a manual fleetwide bump. Remove when action-setup/corepack reliably installs pnpm >=11.9.

TypeScript 7 (the Go-based tsgo compiler) is rejected by typescript-eslint — every fleet CI hard-errors with 'typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0.' (seen on the 2026-08-03 weekly batch: hedloc#27, caltex-landing#45). Keep TS on 6.x until typescript-eslint ships TS7 support, then delete this rule.

@libsql/kysely-libsql (the Kysely dialect reddoor-maintenance's hybrid DB runs on) hard-depends on @libsql/client ^0.8.0 and has no release supporting anything newer, so bumping the direct @libsql/client dep forks the tree into two incompatible Client types (typecheck: 'Promise<Replicated> is not assignable to Promise<void>', reddoor-maintenance#492 on the 2026-08-03 batch). Hold the client at 0.8.x until a kysely-libsql release widens its client range — Renovate will propose that release when it exists, and that PR is the cue to delete this rule and take both bumps together.

cookie v2 removed the parse/serialize named exports that every current @sveltejs/kit (<=2.70.2, cookie dep ^0.6.0) imports — forcing it via the vuln-wave overrides breaks the server build (rollup: 'parse is not exported by cookie@2.0.1', seen fleet-wide 2026-08-03). Worse, the range-WIDENING variant of the bump ('>=0.7.0 <3') is a delayed bomb: it stays on 0.7.x until the next lockfile-maintenance regen, then silently resolves to 2.x. Hold cookie below 2 until kit itself supports it, then delete this rule.

pnpm overrides are hand-managed security pins, never Renovate's to bump. Renovate misreads override KEYS as dependencies and proposes rewriting the pinned range itself: the 2026-08-03 'brace-expansion@<X to v5' wave (widening the override to <6 breaks minimatch@3/9 at runtime) and the 2026-08-10 'cookie@<0.7.0 to v1' wave (17 PRs fleet-wide; cookie 0.7.2 is already fully patched for GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x, so the rewrite adds zero security value and either flips @sveltejs/kit onto untested cookie 1.x or defers that jump to the next lockfile refresh). All three depTypes are listed because the npm manager assigns 'pnpm-workspace.overrides' to pnpm-workspace.yaml override entries (including flat 'parent>child' selector keys like '@sveltejs/kit>cookie'), 'pnpm.overrides' to package.json pnpm.overrides, and 'overrides' to package.json overrides; matching only 'overrides' would miss the workspace-YAML pins the fleet actually uses (pnpm 11 reads overrides from pnpm-workspace.yaml).
